While the text does not use explicit bechina language to equate these Torahs with another concept, they are the positive anchor of the teaching — the domain of pure, luminous Torah light that gets covered. The 'coverings and concealments' (חִפּוּיִים וְהַסְתָּרוֹת) that fall upon sublime Torahs when they are printed as a book are the negative force in this teaching. The text treats them as the concealment of light — a function analogous to the evil domain throughout Likutay Moharan, where הַסְתָּרָה (concealment/hiding) is consistently opposed to אוֹר (light). The binding pages (דַּפִּין שֶׁל כְּרִיכָה) are described as the instrument of this covering. This node is absent from the dataset.

analysis_notes.bechina_in_source_text: The source text contains no word 'בְּחִינַת' and no formal bechina equation. The closest structural equivalence implied (though not stated with bechina language) is: תּוֹרוֹת גְּבוֹהוֹת = אוֹר צַח וְנִפְלָא (the sublime Torahs ARE their luminous light — their essence is that light). However, the Rebbe does not use explicit bechina language to state this; the light is described as belonging to the Torahs ('אוֹרָם'), making it a possessive description rather than a formal bechina equation.
analysis_notes.torah_structure: LM2 Torah 36 is a two-sentence saying (fragment). Its single conceptual move is: (1) Sublime, wondrous Torahs exist whose light is pure and wondrous. (2) [Eitza:] As soon as these Torahs are compiled into a printed book, coverings and concealments fall upon them and their light is hidden. (3) Specifically, the binding pages are what cause the covering. The structure is entirely eitza (cause → effect: bookbinding → concealment of light) with no formal bechina equations. The teaching has a mirror structure: holy luminous Torah vs. the covered/concealed Torah, but this is expressed descriptively rather than through bechina language.
